formula_or_input: Overview:  This worksheet is intended to provide you with visibility into your sales and marketing activities.  This model helps you examine four business scenarios that can help you improve your business performance: increase the size of your sales force, increase your sales organization’s close rate, decrease your sales cycle time, or increase your average order size. By entering historical and assumptive data, you will be able to determine the impact of each of these investment decisions on your top line revenue and bottom line performance.  For example, a 10% decrease in your sales force, coupled with a 10% improvement in your average order size could increase your top line revenue by 7%, but increase your operating margin by almost 800%.  Finally, this tool will help you identify the challenges you must overcome to achieve success in each of the business scenarios and provide you with a better framework to assess current and future sales and marketing investments.

formula_or_input: 3)  Desperation by management to close quarterly revenue
value: 3)  Desperation by management to close quarterly revenue

formula_or_input: Vendors always need to close business to meet quarterly expectations.  This issue becomes a problem when there are not enough opportunities being worked in the pipeline at any given time.  We believe the underlying cause of this desperation is a woefully inadequate internal pipeline management and forecasting reporting process.  Most companies find out far too late what their revenue targets are going to be and thus the end of each quarter becomes a scramble for business.

formula_or_input: 5)  Product pricing doesn't align to the customer's value received
value: 5)  Product pricing doesn't align to the customer's value received

formula_or_input: Often, the pricing model or strategy of a vendor can limit its ability to realize the maximum value of a sales transaction.  There are many pricing models (perpetual licenses, annual licenses, server-based pricing, user-based pricing, leasing, activity-based pricing, etc.)  The point is that your pricing strategy must be oriented to how a customer will realize the benefits of your offering  - so they evaluate the offer more in their context.
